newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: VA Stahl sees more second half woes.
newsitem.headline: VA Stahl sees more second half woes.

text.p: Austrian steelmaker VA Stahl on Friday rattled investors by reporting a 31 percent drop in first-half pretax profit and said it expected more woes before business picked up.

"Our second half will not be as good as the first," said chief executive Peter Strahammer, citing price pressures on short-term contracts and the temporary closure for refurbishment of a plant in Linz as reasons for slower growth.
He said prices were expected to bottom out in the third quarter. "But we expect a significant pick up in demand in the fourth quarter," he added.

The group said pretax earnings in the six months to June slumped to 1.33 billion schillings ($125.1 million) in the first six months to June 30. Turnover fell to 15.99 billion schillings against 17.23 schillings for the year-ago period.
"The pressure on prices and volumes that began at the end of the first quarter in 1995 resulted in a tangible downswing, rather than a dip as we originally expected," the company said.
VA Stahl attributed the decline in part to a surplus of client stocks and a reduction in investment by European governments trying to meet the tight budget criteria for European Monetary Union.
Net profit in the first half slipped to 1.03 billion schillings, compared with 1.64 billion a year ago.
VA Stahl's shares tumbled three percent to 320 schillings on the news but rebounded later in the session to close up three percent at 340 in a marginally weaker Vienna market.
Strahammer said the 1996 full year result would be "slightly better than 1994", when the company posted pre-tax earnings of 1.32 billion schillings and a net profit of 649 million.
But he would not rule out a reduction in the 1996 dividend from last year's 13 schillings per share.
"We will keep our basic dividend at 10 (schillings) and distribute an additional bonus payment. I can't say today whether this bonus will be three (schillings) as it was last year," Strahammer said.
"We estimate that 1997 will on the whole be comparable with 1996," he added. ($1=10.63 Schilling)
